question: In a cohort study comparing a group of subjects with hypertension and a group of subjects with normal blood pressure, an annual incidence of acute myocardial infarction of 15 per thousand and 5 per thousand, respectively, is obtained. Assuming there are no biases or confounding factors, what would be the risk of acute myocardial infarction attributable to hypertension among hypertensive subjects ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hypertension -> increased risk of acute myocardial infarction -> higher annual incidence among hypertensive subjects -> 15 per thousand per year -> 100%
enhanced_information: Hypertension is associated with an increased risk of acute myocardial infarction. The annual incidence of acute myocardial infarction is 15 per thousand among hypertensive subjects and 5 per thousand among those with normal blood pressure. Therefore, the risk of acute myocardial infarction attributable to hypertension among hypertensive subjects is 10 per thousand per year.
analysis: Hypertension is associated with an increased risk of acute myocardial infarction. The annual incidence of acute myocardial infarction is 15 per thousand among hypertensive subjects and 5 per thousand among those with normal blood pressure. The risk of acute myocardial infarction attributable to hypertension among hypertensive subjects can be calculated by subtracting the incidence rate in normal blood pressure subjects from the incidence rate in hypertensive subjects, which gives 15 - 5 = 10 per thousand per year.
